hook_text: You see where a point started and where it landed. Two questions tell you exactly what happened.
clip_script: The point 3 semicolon 5 has moved, and you have to name the move. Question one: did the numbers swap? Question two: which signs flipped? 3 semicolon negative 5: no swap, second sign flipped, a mirror in the x-axis. 5 semicolon 3: swap only, a mirror in the line y equals x. Negative 3 semicolon negative 5: both signs flipped, a half turn. Negative 5 semicolon 3: swap and the first is negative, a quarter turn anticlockwise. If nothing swaps or flips neatly, it slid: work out end minus start. But beware the tricky points. 2 semicolon negative 2 going to negative 2 semicolon 2 could be a swap or a half turn. Check a second corner and the answer is certain. Swap, signs, second point.
visual_style: A single point on a grid with six ghost images lighting up one at a time, each labelled with its move; a tricky point flashes two labels until a second point settles it.
pacing: One fingerprint per beat, a pause on the tricky point, a snap when the second point decides.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for full descriptions, combined moves and the five common errors.
